designSummary: Cluster randomised trial, 16 wards in 8 pairs, analysed at the opportunity level with ward as the cluster.
sampleSize: With 8 wards per arm, about 300 observed opportunities per ward, an intracluster correlation of 0.06 (median of the retrieved estimates, range 0.04 to 0.09) and compliance near 60 percent, the design effect is about 19. Using a t distribution with 14 degrees of freedom, the trial has 80 percent power at two-sided alpha 0.05 to detect a difference of about 18 percentage points, or about 15 points after adjustment for ward baseline compliance. The corrected report of the retrieved trial now gives a 3-point difference on the system's measure, far below what 16 wards can detect, so the planning basis must be re-reviewed before the decision is acted on.
primaryAnalysis: Mixed-effects logistic regression of observed hand hygiene on arm with a random intercept for ward, adjusted for ward baseline compliance and specialty, with small-sample degrees-of-freedom correction; the difference is reported as a risk difference with its confidence interval.
secondaryAnalysis: The same model for badge-system compliance; the difference between badge and observed compliance by arm; hand rub consumption per 1,000 patient-days; float and non-float staff reported separately.
missingData: Unobserved sessions are rescheduled within the same month; wards that lose more than 20 percent of sessions are reported, and no opportunity is imputed.
multiplicity: One primary comparison; secondary outcomes reported with confidence intervals and no significance claims.
software: R with lme4; allocation sequence and analysis code held by the trial statistician.
overfittingGuards: Two adjustment variables fixed in advance
No subgroup testing beyond the float staff split
Allocation concealed from ward managers until switch-on
summary: About 15 points detectable with baseline adjustment; the corrected planning value is far smaller, so the design needs re-review.
